short: The last major battle of the war, in which a combined Franco-Swedish army destroyed the final Imperial rearguard.
full:
On 17 May 1648, a combined Franco-Swedish army commanded by Carl Gustaf Wrangel and the Viscount of Turenne caught the retreating Imperial and Bavarian army near Zusmarshausen in Swabia. The Imperial commander, Peter Melander, attempted to withdraw his forces while leaving a strong rearguard under Raimondo Montecuccoli to delay the pursuers.

The Franco-Swedish vanguard engaged the rearguard in a running, intense firefight that lasted throughout the day. Melander was killed in the action, and while the bulk of the Imperial army escaped total destruction, they lost most of their artillery and baggage. The defeat neutralized the last significant Habsburg field army in Germany, removing any remaining military obstacles to concluding the peace treaties.
